newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Cocoa market capped as strong pound tempts origins.
newsitem.headline: Cocoa market capped as strong pound tempts origins.

text.p: Cocoa traders in Europe said on Thursday the strong British pound was to blame for keeping a lid on futures and physical markets, offering French franc-related origins healthy returns and discouraging industry offtake.
"The market is wedged in. Every time we get up above 1,000 stg (basis London March futures) there is origin selling into the market," one trader said. "It's very attractive for them."
Sterling has steadily moved higher against the franc since early August and is now well above eight francs to the pound, a level not seen since early 1995.
"Industry buyers are naturally cautious but they are looking at the market and having to pay five or six percent more than they would have done a month or two ago," another trader said.
German processors this week cited currency factors behind them not taking on beans for late 1996, early 1997.
A trader said Ivorian shippers were offering bulk Nov/Dec cocoa at 10 stg under Dec futures, with bids at 15 stg under.

The physical market was still waiting for the start of Ivorian arrivals, which traders said they expected after the end of this month. Traders said crop forecasts for the Ivory Coast still centred at, or a little below, one million tonnes.
They said around 350,000 tonnes was predicted to have arrived by the end of the year.
These higher forecasts were behind a general bearish tone in the market, backed up by industry's lack of participation.
"But if the crop comes in around 100,000 tonnes less, then we could see things turned around," one trader said.

Bulk shipments will again figure highly for the major Dutch grinders in the coming season. Gerkens Cacao, a unit of U.S. trade house Cargill, will ship cocoa in bulk mainly from the Ivory Coast but also probably from Ghana, although no deals have yet been signed there, industry sources said.

Logistical problems with current loading facilities and difficulties in getting investment into the country were blamed for the problems over getting bulk started, despite enthusiasm on the part of local shippers.

They contradicted reports sourced to local shipping agents that Gerkens would seek to move its first bulk deal from Ghana this season. Sources said the company was looking to transport bulk from Ghana but added that a large quantity was shipped in containers last season.

But they confirmed that Gerkens had chartered a number of vessels for the coming season to bulk ship cooca from the Ivory Coast in quantities of between 3,000 and 5,000 tonnes a time, with the first vessel due in Amsterdam around mid-November. --Amsterdam Noewsroom +31 20 504 5000
